active_themes.label: Warsh's Impossible Choice — Now Public
active_themes.summary: Hammack's public hike warning today broke the Fed's internal consensus facade. Warsh is cutting into flat demand and 3.4% inflation; Hammack is signaling the opposite policy path should price pressure persist. This is no longer a private debate—it's visible policy conflict. Warsh must now choose within the next two weeks whether to pause cuts (admitting error) or continue and accept the stagflation label. The bond market has already priced this negatively; the equity repricing is still ahead.

active_themes.label: Hostilities Flare, Oil Momentum Shifts
active_themes.summary: Iran-US tensions escalated today with hostile air defenses and US Hellfire missile strikes on a tanker reportedly heading to Iran. Oil jumped on the news but closed modestly up. The deal narrative that dominated last week is now competing with active military engagement. If negotiations collapse in the next 48 hours (as previously warned), oil will spike to $95+. If a deal is announced instead, oil retreats and Warsh gets tactical breathing room—but only tactical. Either way, the next 72 hours are outcome-determinant.

active_themes.label: Credit Tightening Window Narrowing
active_themes.summary: Today's silence from Discover, Capital One, and Amex on deposit rate cuts extends the 5-10 day timeline but does not change it. Flat May spending (0% MoM) gives them institutional cover to announce tightening any day this week. If they remain silent through Friday, it signals they believe weakness is transitory—a bet the data does not support. The first announcement will trigger a 3-5 day equity reset downward as the feedback loop becomes explicit.

active_themes.label: Binary Resolved, Wrong Direction
active_themes.summary: The May 29 spending print (0% MoM) confirmed the second scenario: institutional withdrawal was justified and soft landing is no longer the base case. Today's modest market gains reflect intraday tactical relief on Iran and AI, not conviction about macro. Equities have not yet repriced this fully and face a reset over the next 3-5 days as the credit tightening becomes explicit.

active_themes.label: Stagflation Pricing In
active_themes.summary: Today's flat spending + 3.4% inflation validates the stagflation scenario: Warsh is cutting rates into a demand-weakening environment while inflation remains elevated. The 30-year yield at 2007 highs reflects this and is unlikely to move lower absent a hard demand shock. Long-duration investors are positioned for extended elevated rates; expect 10-year yields to hold 3.9-4.1% range through next data cycle.

active_themes.label: Fed Conflict Now Public; Yields Anchored High
active_themes.summary: Hammack's hike warning validates the stagflation scenario and eliminates any remaining narrative room for Warsh to cut his way out of this cleanly. Long-duration yields at 2007 highs are correctly priced. The 10-year will hold 3.9-4.1% range until demand destruction becomes undeniable or inflation rolls over—neither is happening yet. Warsh is losing the inflation narrative advantage he held three weeks ago.
